llm.summary: The skill mostly matches a validator/ RPC-read project, but there are multiple mismatches between the description/instructions and what it requires or encourages (notably a required Anthropic API key for read-only queries, implicit GitHub/CLI actions that need credentials, and auto-update/peer-binary behavior that deserves review).

dimensions.detail: The skill advertises two distinct capabilities: (A) read-only RPC queries (no auth, no downloads) and (B) optionally running a validator that requires an AI provider key. Despite the read-only path requiring no credentials, registry metadata marks ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as a required/primary env var. Requiring an Anthropic key for what the description says can be done with just curl is disproportionate. The codebase supports multiple AI providers, yet metadata forces a single provider as required. There is also a license mismatch: top-level docs claim MIT but Cargo.toml sets LicenseRef-Proprietary — inconsistent metadata that should be resolved.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays mostly on-scope: public RPC examples use curl and require no keys; validator instructions clearly require an AI API key and building/running the node. However contributor docs instruct AI agents to use the GitHub CLI (gh) to fork, comment, create PRs, and even merge — actions that implicitly require GitHub credentials or elevated permissions but those credentials are not declared in requires.env. The docs also describe auto-updates and P2P binary seeding — behavior that could cause execution of binaries received from peers; the instructions tell users to audit the code but also encourage running auto-update features. Overall instructions are explicit but grant broad operational discretion (network bindings, exposing RPC, running validators, performing repo operations) that may require additional credentials and risk assessment.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec, so nothing is written to disk by the registry installer. The runtime docs recommend building from source or downloading GitHub release binaries (standard practice). No high-risk remote download URLs or obscure hosts are embedded in the registry metadata. The skill does reference running external CLIs (cargo, gh, vercel, docker) — expected for a project of this type.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is declared as required/primary, but the code supports multiple AI providers (OpenAI, Groq, Together, Ollama) and the docs reference additional credentials (OPENAI_API_KEY, gsk_xxx, etc.). Declaring Anthropic as required forces users who only want read-only RPC access (which needs no key) to provide an AI key. Contributor and deployment workflows implicitly need other secrets (GitHub token, Vercel env vars, Docker registry creds) yet those are not declared. Asking for a cloud AI API key is reasonable for running a validator, but the registry-level required-env setting should reflect that it is optional for read-only use or list other credentials if repo operations are expected.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not flagged always:true and does not request persistent installation from the registry (instruction-only). However the project itself implements behavior that has persistence/privilege implications if you run it: it recommends binding RPC/P2P to 0.0.0.0, running background validator processes, exposing ports, and describes an auto-update mechanism and P2P binary seeding. Those runtime features require careful review before enabling auto-updates or public bindings. Autonomous agent invocation is allowed by default (normal) — combine that with the docs encouraging agents to act on GitHub and it increases the risk profile unless the platform mediates credential use.

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing or running this skill:

- Decide your goal: If you only want read-only RPC queries, you should not need to provide an AI API key. The registry metadata marks ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as required — verify with the platform whether that key is actually mandatory for read-only use or only required to run a validator. Do not expose your Anthropic (or other) API key unless you intend to run a validator locally.

- Audit auto-update & P2P binary seeding: The project mentions auto-updates and relaying binaries to peers. If you run a validator, inspect code paths that fetch and execute updates and confirm they verify signatures (the repo includes operator keys metadata, but you should confirm signature verification in the implementation) before enabling auto-updates.

- Be careful with credentials beyond what's declared: contributor docs instruct use of the GitHub CLI and Vercel/Docker flows which implicitly require GitHub/Vercel/Docker credentials. The skill metadata does not list those env vars — do not allow the agent to perform repo operations or push credentials unless you explicitly trust and provision the necessary tokens.

- Verify data flows: The AI client code sends requests directly to provider APIs (e.g., api.anthropic.com) using provided keys. That is expected for an AI-backed validator, but if you have a policy against exposing keys to third-party processes, do not set them here. The project claims API keys "stay local"; confirm that the binary does not log or broadcast keys and that P2P messages never include secrets.

- License & provenance: Resolve the license inconsistency (README vs Cargo.toml) and prefer running from source (audit code) rather than downloading unreviewed binaries.

- If you plan to run a validator:
  - Run it on an isolated host or VM with limited privileges and firewall rules (only expose ports you trust).
  - Keep private key (keypair.json) offline and never upload it. The docs repeat this; follow it.
  - Monitor network activity and audit the node logs for unexpected outgoing connections.

If you want, I can: (a) point out the exact lines in the source that perform AI API calls and auto-update checks, (b) search the repo for any code that logs or includes 'api_key' or other sensitive identifiers, or (c) draft a minimal safe-run checklist (firewall, env var scoping, build-from-source steps).
